symbol_repair_2026_11_08.why: docx_text() read only w:t, w:tab, w:br/w:cr and w:noBreakHyphen, so it dropped every Word <w:sym> character. This compilation writes 809 symbols in the coordinates of Schedule 1 (Torres Strait Treaty) as Symbol-font w:sym elements: 785 second signs (F0B2, ″), 12 degree signs (F0B0, °) and 12 minute signs (F0A2, ′). They were dropped with nothing in their place, so a coordinate such as "Latitude 25° 56′ 54.5515″ South" read "Latitude 25 56 54.5515 South". cth_convert_sym_v5n.py maps them to their Unicode characters. The Word file has no private-use code points.
symbol_repair_2026_11_08.what_changed: 809 characters restored on 694 lines of Schedule 1 (Torres Strait Treaty), lines 1646-2969, nothing else: Article 1 paragraph 2 (line 1646, the Johnston Geodetic Station, "Latitude 25° 56′ 54.5515″ South and at Longitude 133° 12′ 30.0771″ East"), Article 3 paragraph 6 (lines 1672-1673), Article 4 paragraph 3 (line 1680), and the points and lines of Annex 1 (territorial sea boundaries, 15 lines, 1923-1939), Annex 3 (outer limits of territorial seas, 605 lines, 1950-2888), Annex 5 (seabed jurisdiction line, 21 lines, 2892-2912), Annex 8 (fisheries jurisdiction line, 35 lines, 2916-2950) and Annex 9 (protected zone, 14 lines, 2954-2969). 785 second signs (″), 12 degree signs (°), 12 minute signs (′). Where the Word file types minutes and seconds as acute accents (´, ´´) in ordinary text (776 of them), those were never lost and are unchanged. Line count (4360) is unchanged; character count 370662 -> 371471.
